selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the first special gain a gardener can receive if the gardener works with a good intention?
questions.answer: The gardener can share in the reward of the worship made by the plants and trees he grows.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect a person with the praise made by plants and trees?
questions.answer: Because the person helped grow them with the right intention.

questions.question: What is the second “mine” really about?
questions.answer: It is about the garden’s produce becoming like charity when used in the right way.

questions.question: What protects a person from misunderstanding this wide reward?
questions.answer: The reminder that the person must work for Allah and stay within what Allah permits.

questions.question: What part do trees and plants play in the worker’s reward?
questions.answer: Their acts of praise become a source of shared reward for him.

questions.question: What is the effect of abandoning the required prayers on these two “mines”?
questions.answer: The person is cut off from their benefits.

questions.question: How does losing those gains affect a person’s energy and attitude?
questions.answer: It weakens his desire to work and lowers his spirit.

questions.question: What future-focused goal gives the other man strength?
questions.answer: He wants benefit for his grave and the hereafter.

questions.question: What words show that this person’s problem is not only physical tiredness?
questions.answer: He also loses heart and falls into idleness.

questions.question: Which kind of activities does the other man want to increase?
questions.answer: He wants to increase acts of worship and lawful daily work.

questions.question: In the passage, what does having a sound intention do for someone working in a garden?
questions.answer: It turns ordinary gardening into a way to gain reward.

questions.question: What is the first “mine” really about?
questions.answer: It is about gaining hidden spiritual reward through sincere intention.

questions.question: Does the passage limit this benefit only to people who buy the produce fairly?
questions.answer: No. The benefit is described much more widely, including many kinds of eaters.

questions.question: Why is a good intention so important in the passage?
questions.answer: It changes normal work into worshipful reward.

questions.question: What attitude about ownership is the worker told to have?
questions.answer: He should think of himself as a servant delivering Allah’s gifts.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does a person lose by leaving the required prayers?
questions.answer: He loses great spiritual riches and misses the two valuable gains.

questions.question: What emotional result comes to the prayerless person over time?
questions.answer: He becomes discouraged and loses the will to continue.

questions.question: How does old age affect the person who leaves prayer in this passage?
questions.answer: It makes his weariness and loss of interest even worse.

questions.question: How does the second man view hard work differently?
questions.answer: He sees it as a way to prepare for what comes after death.

questions.question: Why does the other man want to work harder?
questions.answer: He wants to send more light to his grave and prepare more for the life to come.

questions.question: What work setting is used in the passage to teach a lesson?
questions.answer: A garden and the work done in it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about produce eaten by many different kinds of creatures and people?
questions.answer: It can count like charity from the worker.

questions.question: What is promised to the one who grows plants with the right intention?
questions.answer: He gains spiritual reward connected to the worship of what he grows.

questions.question: How is the other man different in his response?
questions.answer: He chooses to work more in worship and in lawful work.
